ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input ( #28738 )

- ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input

The GEMM behind conv_1d folds the batch into its rows, so the product

sits in memory as [OL, N, OC] while the reshape claims [OL, OC, N].

The shape is right and the contents are transposed, so nothing fires:

no assert, no abort, the graph just runs and the channels come out

interleaved with the batches. With N == 1 the two readings describe

the same buffer, which is why the three vocoders in the tree never

hit it, they all squeeze to 2d right after the call.

Reshape to the real layout and permute OC and N back. The N == 1 path

keeps its direct reshape, so the current callers build the same graph

and pay for no extra copy.

tests/test-conv-1d.cpp compares one batched convolution against N

single batch convolutions built from the same weight and the same

input slices. Five of the seven geometries fail before this change and

all seven pass after. N == 1 and OC == 1 pass either way, since

swapping two dimensions when one of them is 1 changes nothing.

The batched path matters to downstream audio projects where several

synthesis lanes share a single graph. Nothing in mtmd batches a

vocoder today, each one streams one flow and carries its left context

between calls, but the op is correct now if one of them grows a lane

- ggml: build the same conv_1d graph for every batch size

Address review from ggerganov: drop the N == 1 branch of ggml_conv_1d.

The GEMM result is always reshaped to [OC, N, OL] and permuted back,

as ggml_conv_2d does, so every batch size builds the same graph. For

N == 1 this adds a cont on an already ordered tensor.
